acceptance: A survey of `fetchone(` and of error handling inside open transactions on DuckDB connections under `benchbox/` is listed in this item with each site marked safe or fixed.
The skipped index bound-form test has a 2.x equivalent or a recorded reason it cannot.
The Arrow fetch uses the supported 2.x API where the runtime provides it, and the warning filter is removed or justified.
User documentation states which BenchBox-written DuckDB files are not readable by DuckDB 1.x after running on 2.x.
The `tpcds_answers()` error is reproduced and reported upstream, or explained.

2026-11-13 15:29 EST: pull request https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4212 (branch fix/duckdb-2-behaviour-audit, head 1e984c200f) is open and waiting on CI; local `make pr-preflight` passed (8744 passed, 31 skipped). One hosted-review Medium finding (Arrow mode used the relation path only for SELECT/WITH) was fixed and its thread resolved.

Survey: 281 `fetchone()` call sites in 61 files. Not a DuckDB connection: 187. DuckDB and safe (followed only by execute/DDL/DML, a fresh per-operation connection, or a closed connection): 72. DuckDB and at risk (a SELECT result left unfinished on a long-lived shared connection that can later reach a register call): 22.
Observed on DuckDB 2.0.0: an unread `fetchone()` (even of a one-row result), or a SELECT executed and never fetched, leaves the result unfinished and blocks `register()`, `sql()` and `table()` with ResourceInUseException; a plain `execute()`, `cursor()`, commit or rollback clears it; DML counts finish at once; `connection.complete()` is DuckDB's remedy.
Disposition of the 22: mitigated at the sinks, producers unchanged. New helper `finish_unfinished_result` (benchbox/utils/duckdb_extensions.py) calls `complete()` before the three places that use the blocked APIs: `bulk_insert_dataframe` (benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/sql_backend.py), `insert_arrow_table` (benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py), and the Arrow fetch in `execute_query` (benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py) with `fetch_duckdb_arrow_table`. Regression tests in tests/unit/platforms/test_duckdb_unfinished_results.py. No product-path failure could be reproduced at any of the 22 sites. At-risk sites: benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/sql_backend.py:353,363,386,393,401,410,414,418; benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/data_quality_monitor.py:171,206,223,253,277,294,312; benchbox/core/tpcdi/loader.py:213,225,289; benchbox/core/tpcdi/validation.py:236; benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/pipeline.py:143; benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py:1407,1413.

Transactions: on 2.0.0 parser, catalog and constraint errors abort an explicit transaction; conversion errors do not. Fixed: `EnhancedSCDType2Processor._transaction` (benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/scd_processor.py) no longer sends SAVEPOINT, which DuckDB cannot parse, into a caller-owned transaction. No other site was found that catches a SQL error and continues in the same open DuckDB transaction.
Arrow fetch: on 2.x every Arrow-mode statement goes through `con.sql(query).to_arrow_table()` after `complete()`, gated on the running version; older runtimes keep `fetch_arrow_table`; the warning filter is removed.
Skipped index test: a 2.x equivalent asserts the index expression is stored as written and corroborated; the bound-form test is skipped on 2.x only.
File format: documented in README.md. Not readable by 1.x once created by 2.x: `.duckdb` platform databases and `.wal` files, DuckLake `metadata.ducklake` catalogs, `_write_primitives_df_parity.duckdb`. Unaffected: result JSON, the SQLite results store, Parquet/CSV data, the Explorer snapshot.
`tpcds_answers()`: raises `Don't have TPC-DS answers for SF 10.000000!` on 2.0.0 and on 1.5.5 regardless of the scale factor loaded; not a 2.0 regression. Reproduction: connect, INSTALL tpcds, LOAD tpcds, `select count(*) from tpcds_answers()`. Not reported upstream by the agent; that is left to the owner.
Open point for the owner: whether the DuckDB page in benchbox-site should carry the file-format note.

description:
Gap. The DuckDB 2.x pin lift (PR #4175) fixed each DuckDB 2.0 break that a test exposed. Several are behaviour changes that product code could hit on paths no test covers:
- A parser error inside a caller's open transaction now aborts the transaction. Only a SAVEPOINT test was adjusted (it now rolls back first). Any code that catches a SQL error and continues in the same transaction is affected.
- An unfinished result from `fetchone()` blocks later use of the connection (seen in the TPC-DI customer batch loader, where it blocked DataFrame `register`). Other `fetchone()` calls on DuckDB connections were not surveyed.
- `fetch_arrow_table` and `Relation.fetchone()` are removed; DuckDB warns `Arrow output on a DB-API result` on every Arrow fetch and BenchBox now suppresses that one warning around its fetch instead of moving to the replacement API.
- Index expressions are stored unbound; the bound-form mismatch test is skipped on 2.x, so that check has no coverage on the locked version.
- Database files written by 2.x cannot be opened by 1.x. The explorer snapshot is pinned to the old storage format; other persisted DuckDB files (result stores, cached benchmark databases) are not, and a user who downgrades or shares them loses access. This is disclosed in the changelog only.
- `tpcds_answers()` in DuckDB's `tpcds` extension raised `Don't have TPC-DS answers for SF 10.0` during an SF1 check, so answers were compared 2.0 against 1.5.5 instead of against published answers.

Expected: each bullet has a recorded disposition: code fixed, test coverage restored on 2.x, documented as a limitation, or reported upstream.

Guardrails: do not regenerate digests or baselines. Keep older runtimes selected through `driver_version` working. No change to SQL query text to work around engine behaviour without recording why.
